comments.text: What stayed with me is how the whole video is built around the chitenge as a document of a life — the first ride on a mother's back, the naming chapter where your name tells everyone the story of the day you arrived, and the marketplace stalls where women choose their prints. I had no idea Japanese prints reached Zambia through the Congo by the 1930s — a whole trade history folded into two yards of cloth. The best episode of yours I've watched so far.

comments.text: The chitenge is a great example of how an everyday object can carry far more meaning than its practical use suggests. 🇿🇲🧵 It can become clothing, a baby carrier, a ceremonial symbol and part of major family events throughout a person’s life. Objects like this reveal culture in a way that monuments often cannot, because they remain part of ordinary daily routines.
